rationale: Bug-fix scope, reviewed against the branch diff (docs/superpowers/tasks/2026-07-30-gitlab-mr-action-from-object-attributes/code-review.diff): 2 source files, 2 test files, 292 insertions. The defect is real and the fix is minimal and correct. extract_mr_action now reads object_attributes.action (src/codemie/triggers/bindings/gitlab_webhook_security.py:73-80), which is where GitLab actually puts it, and keeps a top-level fallback for custom webhook templates; object_attributes takes precedence when both are present. Parsing was de-duplicated onto the pre-existing _parse_body (line 83), which returns {} on decode/JSON failure or a non-dict payload, so the dict / str / bytes paths converge and a malformed body degrades to 'not a merge_request event' exactly as before — no new exception path. object_attributes is guarded with isinstance before .get, so a payload with a non-dict object_attributes cannot raise. Behaviour for non-MR events is unchanged (validate_mr_event_type still passes them through). Test-first was genuinely followed: moving action into object_attributes turned 12 pre-existing tests RED against the old implementation (19 failed / 99 passed, recorded in plan.md Task 1) before the extractor was touched, which proves the defect rather than asserting it; 118 passed after the fix. The conftest fixtures now mirror a verified GitLab 17.11.7 delivery (labels, changes, repository added, no top-level action), which removes the blind spot that let 111 binding tests pass against broken code. 7 regression tests cover object_attributes extraction, top-level fallback, precedence, unknown action, allowed/blocked filtering on real payloads, and the raw-bytes path. Documentation was corrected in the same change: docs/webhook-configuration.md no longer claims a filtered action returns 400 and now states the deliberate 200 ACK plus the reason (GitLab auto-disables hooks after repeated non-2xx). No blocking or non-blocking findings; no scoped confirmation pass required.
